name: NCRB district-wise crimes under IPC (Crime in India district supplementary tables), Bihar extract 2001-2014
publisher: National Crime Records Bureau, Ministry of Home Affairs, via Open Government Data Platform India (data.gov.in)
geo_coverage: all-India; Bihar extract used here (44 police districts)
caveats: NCRB principal offence rule: only the most serious offence in a multi-offence FIR is counted, so every non-apex head is systematically undercounted and the undercount is worse in high-violence areas
Geography is the POLICE district that registered the FIR, not where the offence occurred
Bihar units are 40 territorial police districts + 4 railway GRP units; railway units have no polygon in our thana spine and must never be dissolved into territory
NCRB names two districts by HQ town: BETTIAH = West Champaran, MOTIHARI = East Champaran. A naive string join drops both
TOTAL / ZZ TOTAL rows are embedded in the data and double-count the state if not dropped
2014 file is a schema break: 93 columns vs 33, 'Railway' not 'RLY.', and adds Anti Terrorist Squad + Economic Offences Unit as non-geographic pseudo-districts
Series ends 2014; NCRB additionally withheld district data entirely for reference years 2016 and 2017
Column names carry NCRB's own misspellings (COUNTERFIETING, HURT/GREVIOUS HURT) - preserve them or the join to a head dictionary breaks
Pre-BNS taxonomy throughout; unusable as a continuous series across the 2024-07-01 IPC-to-BNS break
Retrieved from a GitHub mirror because data.gov.in is egress-blocked in this environment; the mirror is not the publisher
evidence: Downloaded to data/raw/ncrb-ogd-district/. 01_..._2001_2012.csv is 1,019,080 bytes, 9,018 lines, 33 columns, sha256 590bd77d0c827d68c4370f8ff94b126951ecbf1bd61d5e7dbb6db9fdfb9a6388 - byte-identical across 4 independent repos (PaletiKrishnasai, aadhityasw, and the LFS oid in DMR-001/crime and Prathamesh0-0/KSP-CrimeIntel). 540 Bihar rows (45 units x 12 years); 45 Bihar rows 2013; 47 in 2014. Authenticity test: sum of the 44 Bihar district rows equals the file's own TOTAL row at delta 0 for all 12 years (2001=88,432; 2012=146,614) and for 2013 (167,455).
how_to_obtain: Reachable directly from raw.githubusercontent.com. Canonical source data.gov.in requires an OGD API key and is .gov.in-blocked here.
notes: THE core Bihar find. Joins to data/spine/bihar_stations.csv via data/reference/bihar_ncrb_district_crosswalk.csv with zero unmapped labels in both directions across 2001-2014.

name: NCRB district-wise crimes against women / SC / ST / children, Bihar extract 2001-2014
publisher: National Crime Records Bureau, MHA, via data.gov.in
caveats: Same principal-offence-rule, reporting-office and railway-unit caveats as the IPC table
Crimes against women are among the most under-reported categories; a low district count may mean low reporting, not low incidence - never render as 'safe'
ST table found only for 2013 and 2014; children table only for 2013
SC/ST heads mix IPC offences with SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act offences
Series ends 2014
evidence: Downloaded 42_...women_{2001_2012,2013,2014}, 02_01_...SC_{2001_2012,2013,2014}, 02_...ST_{2013,2014}, 03_...children_2013 to data/raw/ncrb-ogd-district/. Women 2001-2012 file 437,784 bytes with 540 Bihar rows; all 12 years reconcile district-sum to TOTAL row at delta 0. Same 44-unit Bihar geography as the IPC table, so the same crosswalk applies unchanged.
notes: Priority 5 for the women's table specifically: it is the category a public safety map is most often asked about.

name: Bihar NCRB-to-thana-spine police district crosswalk (built in this research)
caveats: Validated against NCRB vocabularies for 2001-2012, 2013 and 2014 only; a 2015+ source may introduce labels not present here - assert on unresolved labels rather than dropping them
Railway rows carry an empty revenue_district by design: a GRP unit is a railway line, not an area
Bagaha and Naugachhia are police districts carved out of West Champaran and Bhagalpur; use the revenue_district column when a 38-district product is needed
Does not carry LGD or Census-2011 district codes - lgdirectory.gov.in was egress-blocked
evidence: 52 rows: 44 mappable police districts, plus the drop-list (TOTAL, ZZ TOTAL, Anti Terrorist Squad, Economic Offences Unit) and the 2014 'Railway' spelling variants. Validated programmatically over 6 NCRB files: zero unmapped NCRB labels, zero spine districts uncovered, in both directions. Six labels genuinely differ from the spine: BETTIAH->WEST CHAMPARAN, MOTIHARI->EAST CHAMPARAN, BHABHUA->KAIMUR (BHABUA), PURNEA->PURNIA, NAWADAH->NAWADA, NAUGACHIA->NAUGACHHIA.
notes: Cross-checked against the independent SCRB district-code vocabulary in scrape_scrb.py, which names the same two units East_Champaran/West_Champaran - that is what confirmed Motihari/Bettiah are the same geography and not missing districts.

name: Bihar State Data Lab - Police & Crime sector (35 XLSX, 2013-2022)
publisher: Government of Bihar, State Data Lab (statedata.bihar.gov.in/dataLab)
caveats: EGRESS-BLOCKED here: statedata.bihar.gov.in is .gov.in and the proxy returns 403 to CONNECT. I have exact URLs but never fetched a file
File titles and years come from a third-party scrape manifest dated 2026-03-27, not from my own listing
Year coverage of 'Districtwise Number of Reported Cases' is gappy: 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2018, 2021, 2022 - 2017, 2019, 2020 absent for that title
Whether the district breakdown is by revenue district (38) or police district (44) is UNKNOWN until a file is opened - this decides which crosswalk column to join on
Definitions are Bihar Police's, not NCRB's; do not concatenate with the NCRB panel without reconciling the 2013-2014 overlap first
XLSX files are served from a directory path called /pdf/
evidence: Downloaded the committed manifest bihar_sectors_all.json (287,937 bytes) from Kantvishu/Govt-of-Bihar-Data and parsed it: 40 sectors, 1,109 files, source 'https://statedata.bihar.gov.in/dataLab/', scrape_date 2026-03-27. Sector 24 'Police & Crime' has 35 files; sector 1 'Civil And Criminal Justice' has 20; sector 20 'Jail' has 102. Extracted 157 crime/justice URLs to data/raw/bihar-statedata/bihar_statedatalab_crime_justice_files.csv. Confirmed blocked: https://statedata.bihar.gov.in/dataLab/ returns HTTP 000 via the proxy.
how_to_obtain: From any unblocked network, curl-loop the download_url column of data/raw/bihar-statedata/bihar_statedatalab_crime_justice_files.csv (157 files). The site's captcha is a front-end modal only and does not gate the asset paths.
notes: Highest-value blocked item for Bihar: machine-readable, district-level, covers 2015-2022 - exactly the gap NCRB's district CSVs leave. Also holds 'Number Of Police Station In Bihar' (2015, 2016, 2018), the official thana roster.

name: Bihar State Data Lab - Status of Trial of Criminal Cases / Cases decided in Sub Courts, 2012-2021
publisher: Government of Bihar, State Data Lab
caveats: EGRESS-BLOCKED; titles known from the third-party manifest only
geo_granularity recorded as 'state' conservatively: the titles do not say whether there is a district breakdown. Upgrade to district only after opening a file
Court disposal is not police disposal - a case disposed by a court is a different denominator from an FIR closed by police
Trial outcomes lag the FIR by years, so a disposal rate joined to a crime-year map is a mismatched vintage
evidence: 20 files in sector 1 'Civil And Criminal Justice' of the manifest: 'Status of Trial of Criminal Cases (YYYY).xlsx' and 'No of Cases decided in Sub Courts of Bihar (YYYY).xlsx', both for each year 2012-2021. URLs captured in data/raw/bihar-statedata/bihar_statedatalab_crime_justice_files.csv.
how_to_obtain: Same curl-loop as the Police & Crime sector.
notes: Closest thing to a disposal series found for Bihar. Jumps to priority 5 if the files turn out to carry a district breakdown.

name: SCRB Bihar FIR / Arrest / Dead-Bodies / Missing-Persons repository - endpoint mechanics and district code table
publisher: State Crime Records Bureau, Bihar Police (mechanics documented by Kantvishu/Govt-of-Bihar-Data)
caveats: EGRESS-BLOCKED here (403 on CONNECT to scrb.bihar.gov.in) - all mechanics below are read from committed third-party code, not exercised by me
Reported record counts (92,424 FIRs, 277,557 arrests) are UNVERIFIABLE: that repo's data/ directory is gitignored and the raw paths 404

Systematic exclusions by design: FIRs debarred by court order, touching national security, or that 'may adversely affect Law & Order and communal situations' are not uploaded - censoring exactly the categories a safety map most wants, non-randomly
An FIR is a report, not a finding: no outcome, and withdrawn or false cases are not retracted

SEVERE PRIVACY HAZARD: names not-yet-convicted accused, and the arrest feed carries officer name + designation. The documenting repo states 35,719 officers are individually identifiable and that surnames permit approximate caste inference
The FIR page's date filter is broken and returns all data regardless of the date parameters
Server is unstable: OutOfMemoryException on large districts, photo-rendering crashes, DNS instability under load
Some districts only joined the system in 2023+, so early-year coverage is uneven across districts
evidence: Read scrape_scrb.py (331 lines) and CLAUDE.md from Kantvishu/Govt-of-Bihar-Data, downloaded to data/raw/bihar-statedata/scrape_scrb.py. Endpoints FIRiew.aspx, ArrestDetail.aspx, deadbodies.aspx, MissingPersons.aspx. ASP.NET postback: GET for __VIEWSTATE/__VIEWSTATEGENERATOR/__EVENTVALIDATION, then POST ctl00$ContentPlaceHolder1$ddlDistrict + txtfDate/txttDate + btnSearch. Carries a 49-entry district code table (40 territorial IDs 1-39,41; 9 special units 42,44,45,46,48,49,50,51,52 = ATS, SVU, 4 Rail units, VIB, Economic_Offence_Unit, CID_Patna).
how_to_obtain: From an unblocked network: GET the page for the ViewState triple, then POST per district with ddlPoliceStation left EMPTY to return the whole district. No login and no captcha; session cookie only. Query by date range to avoid the OutOfMemory crash.
notes: CORRECTS state-police-east-ne.md, which states there is 'no single bulk endpoint'. There is one, per district. Also supplies the SCRB district vocabulary (East_Champaran/West_Champaran) that confirmed NCRB's Motihari/Bettiah mapping. Do not scrape before legal sign-off.

name: NCRB persons arrested and their disposal by police and court (IPC/SLL) and arrests by sex/age - STATE level
publisher: National Crime Records Bureau, MHA, via data.gov.in
caveats: NEGATIVE FINDING RECORDED DELIBERATELY: despite filenames that promise disposal and despite sitting in a directory called 'district', these files are STATE x CRIME HEAD. Column 2 is CRIME HEAD, not DISTRICT. Do not let a later ingest infer district granularity from the path or the filename
Counts PERSONS arrested and disposed, not CASES - a different unit from the crime tables and not divisible by them
Only 2012 and 2013 found for the disposal tables
17_Crime_by_place_of_occurrence is STATE x YEAR (12 Bihar rows for 2001-2012, 1 row each for 2013 and 2014) despite 'place of occurrence' sounding spatial
evidence: Downloaded 04_01 (SLL 2012, 2013), 04_02 (IPC 2012, 2013), 07_01 (arrests by sex/age IPC 2013, 2014) and 17 (place of occurrence 2001-2012, 2013, 2014) to data/raw/ncrb-ogd-district/. Parsed headers: col1 STATE/UT, col2 CRIME HEAD, col3 'Persons in custody or on bail during the stage of investigation at the beginning of the year'. Bihar appears as 30 crime-head rows in 04_02 2013 and 11 in 04_01 2013 - crime heads, not districts.
notes: Answers the case-disposal hunt item with an explicit NO at district level for Bihar. Retained only as a state-level benchmark.

name: devdatalab/paper-justice - eCourts criminal case replication data (5 million cases, 2010-2018)
publisher: Development Data Lab / Ash, Asher, Bhowmick, Chen, Devi, Goessman, Novosad, Siddiqi (2021)
caveats: The repository contains CODE ONLY; the data packet is hosted off-GitHub and every candidate academic host (dataverse.harvard.edu, zenodo.org, osf.io) is egress-blocked here
Court venue is not offence location - a district court's catchment is not a police district
Replication packet needs ~30 GB RAM and Stata 16+ / Matlab per its own README
eCourts coverage is uneven by state and year; Bihar-specific completeness is unverified
Cases, not crimes: an FIR may yield zero, one or many cases, so this cannot be differenced against NCRB counts
evidence: Read the repo README from raw.githubusercontent.com. Names cases_clean_2010 through cases_clean_2018 ('close to the universe of criminal cases in India from 2010-2018'), judges_clean, poi_master, ACLED_India_violence_2005-2023 and acled_districts (a key matching ACLED violence data to Indian districts). Build described in make_justice.do.
how_to_obtain: From an unblocked network, follow the data packet link at the end of the repo README. The authors state they hold permission to use and share the data.
notes: The best available route to district-level COURT disposal for Bihar, which is the gap the NCRB tables leave. Blocked from here, not dismissed.

name: devdatalab/masala-merge - fuzzy matcher tuned for Indian place names
caveats: A tool, not data

Fuzzy matching must not be used for the NCRB district join - that join is exact via the crosswalk, and a fuzzy matcher would happily mis-pair BETTIAH with something wrong. Reserve it for station-name resolution
Requires Stata or R plus Python; $MASALA_PATH and $tmp must be set
evidence: Read README from raw.githubusercontent.com: Levenshtein with costs customised for Indian transliteration (e.g. KS->X), plus Stata reclink content matching; excludes ambiguous matches by default; emits a CSV of unmatched observations for manual review; matches within group variables such as state/district.
notes: Aimed at the 99 needs-review stations and 190 unreached thana polygons in data/spine/crosswalk_report.json.

name: Bihar Police Crime Monitoring Abstract (CMA) - monthly state crime statistics 2010-2021
caveats: DOUBLE-BLOCKED: the legacy host is .nic.in and the only route to it, web.archive.org, is also egress-blocked here
State-level aggregates only, NOT district - attractive cadence, wrong granularity for the map
2016 missing (the archived page was truncated); 2021 covers Jan-Mar only
14 crime categories only, a much coarser taxonomy than NCRB's 30 heads
Live site appears defunct; Wayback is the only route
evidence: Documented in Kantvishu/Govt-of-Bihar-Data CLAUDE.md as 'Bihar Police CMA (Archived)', URL pattern http://biharpolice.bih.nic.in/menuhome/CMA-{YYYY}.htm via the Wayback Machine, yielding a reported 1,848 monthly observations across 14 crime categories for 2010-2021.
how_to_obtain: From an unblocked network, fetch http://web.archive.org/web/*/biharpolice.bih.nic.in/menuhome/CMA-*.htm for each year 2010-2021.
notes: CORRECTS state-police-east-ne.md, which reports that biharpolice.bihar.gov.in 'appears in no index'. The real legacy host is biharpolice.bih.nic.in - a different TLD path, which is why it was missed.

name: Crime in Bihar (SCRB annual volumes) - later years 2021-2024
publisher: State Crime Records Bureau, Bihar Police
caveats: UNVERIFIED: no 2021+ volume was observed by me or by any GitHub mirror; existence inferred from the 2018-2020 series plus State Data Lab Police & Crime files existing for 2021 and 2022
scrb.bihar.gov.in is egress-blocked here
Predecessor volumes are unstructured and partly scanned PDFs in Devanagari - OCR required, machine_readable 1
SCRB's own note on earlier volumes says the data is 'not for legal use'
Any 2024+ volume straddles the IPC-to-BNS break of 2024-07-01
evidence: No GitHub mirror of any Crime in Bihar PDF was found. Searched GitHub repositories and code for 'Crime in Bihar', 'bihar_crime', 'crime_in_bihar': the only Bihar crime repos are Kantvishu/Govt-of-Bihar-Data (scraper, no PDFs) and satishkt/bihar_crime_analysis (2016, empty to code search).
how_to_obtain: From an unblocked network, increment the known filename pattern: https://scrb.bihar.gov.in/images/cib_21.pdf through cib_24.pdf. Fallback: RTI to PIO, SCRB Bihar, Sardar Patel Bhawan, Patna.
notes: Seed lead carried forward from state-police-east-ne.md, now with the negative GitHub result attached so nobody re-runs that search.

name: HAZARD - unsourced and derived 'India crime' CSVs circulating on GitHub
caveats: DO NOT INGEST. Catalogued as a hazard, not a source
A previous agent identified two widely-circulated Kaggle 'India crime' datasets that are outright synthetic

Derived ML outputs are the commonest trap: Xmanish8/KSP_DATATHON's data/processed/ holds ~70 files including risk_scores.csv, crime_forecast.csv, anomaly_flagged.csv and hotspot_clusters.csv - model output presented alongside genuine raw data in the same repo
Most mirrors carry no README provenance at all: of 4 mirror READMEs checked, only PaletiKrishnasai names NCRB and the licence
Renamed copies lose the NN_ OGD table-number prefix that is the only provenance a bare CSV carries
evidence: GitHub repository search for 'NCRB crime india data' returned 57 repos, nearly all student EDA with no stated source; 'crime india district dataset' returned 8. Checked READMEs of 4 mirrors: only PaletiKrishnasai/Analytics_of_crimes_in_India cites 'National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB), Govt of India ... Open Govt Data Platform India portal under Govt. Open Data License - India'. Also observed Git-LFS pointer stubs returning HTTP 200 with a 132-byte body that is not CSV.
how_to_obtain: n/a - this entry exists to stop ingestion.
notes: Two mechanical defences, both cheap: (1) require the NN_ OGD table-number prefix in the filename; (2) run the district-sum-vs-TOTAL-row reconciliation from entry 1 - genuine NCRB extracts reconcile at delta 0, fabricated ones do not. No landing URL is recorded because this entry names a class of files, not a source.
